note: The google-cloud MCP server answers in prose with a row preview; `bq` returns JSON. Requires the emulator started for this task: uv run python server/fakes/gcp.py academic-warning. Every google-cloud projection ends in `grep .`, so an arm whose reply carries no such line fails the case instead of agreeing on nothing.

cases.name: run_query_count
cases.why: the same statement returns the same answer through either arm

args.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM academic_warning.scores_2501

mirage.command: google-cloud bigquery-run-query '{"query":"SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM academic_warning.scores_2501"}'

cases.name: scores_by_student
cases.why: the scores the warning is computed from agree value for value

args.query: SELECT score FROM academic_warning.scores_2501 ORDER BY student_id LIMIT 3

mirage.command: google-cloud bigquery-run-query '{"query":"SELECT score FROM academic_warning.scores_2501 ORDER BY student_id LIMIT 3"}'

cases.name: log_starts_empty
cases.why: the grade counts entries written during the run, so both arms have to start from the same empty log -- and the check that asserts it is skipped silently when the launch timestamp will not parse

mcp.pipe: sed -n 's/^Found \([0-9]*\) log entries.*/\1/p; s/^No log entries found.*/0/p' | grep .

mirage.pipe: sed -n 's/^Found \([0-9]*\) log entries.*/\1/p; s/^No log entries found.*/0/p' | grep .

cases.name: log_bucket_visible
cases.why: the task names its destination by prefix, so both arms must be able to discover the same seeded log bucket through the confined Cloud Logging client
